note: Prototype data. Episodes sampled from data/discover.json and data/session.json; the foray is data/forays.json capital-types-1 joined to data/segments.json. The live foray has no narration items, so the 8 narration gaps (14-18 s each) are a prototype assumption to show the hatched gaps. Round 2: `fr` is a first-run reason written for the prototype (what the pick is for, not what it contains); the Fusion & energy systems subject count is set to 5 to match the direction's find-empty example.

episodes.title: #353 – Dennis Whyte: Nuclear Fusion and the Future of Energy
episodes.hook: Your fusion-reactor tour opens with SPARC's co-founder: every confinement approach, then deep on tokamak magnets.
episodes.own: MIT's Dennis Whyte (Commonwealth Fusion co-founder) on magnetic vs inertial confinement, the Lawson criterion, and how SPARC's REBCO tape magnets differ from ITER's niobium-tin.
episodes.fr: A long, careful guide to fusion energy, for when you want one subject done properly.

episodes.title: The Mystery of Damascus Steel
episodes.hook: You care how fusion-grade alloys behave under stress — ancient smiths solved carbon control completely blind.
episodes.own: The lost crucible-steel process: how ancient smiths achieved hardness and edge retention through carbon control nobody has fully reverse-engineered.
episodes.fr: A short, light story about a lost craft, so you hear what a stretch pick sounds like.

episodes.title: The Assyrians – Empire of Iron
episodes.hook: An empire built on iron metallurgy and siege engineering — your ancient-military itch with a materials spine.
episodes.own: The neo-Assyrian war machine: siege engineering, iron weapons, and administrative innovation — then collapse.
episodes.fr: One empire told start to finish, for when you want history with a plot.

episodes.title: Danny McBride Returns
episodes.hook: Zero homework: Conan and an old friend riffing — dropped yesterday, still warm.
episodes.own: Old friends riffing on cartoons, horror sequels, and McBride's new book.
episodes.fr: Easy talk between old friends, to balance the heavier picks above.
